chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadala from Husayn ibn 'Uthman from Ibn Muskhan and Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskhan from Sulayman ibn Khalid said:
I asked him about what I should say when I lie down on my right side after the two rak'ahs of Fajr.
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Recite the five verses that are at the end of Surah Al-Imran up to "Indeed, you do not break the promise".'
Indeed, you do not break the promise
And say: 'I have held fast to the firmest handhold of Allah, which "has no break".'
And I have taken hold of the strong rope of Allah.
And I seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the transgressors among the Arabs and the non-Arabs.
I have believed in Allah, "I have placed my trust in Allah".
I have placed my trust in Allah
I have leaned my back upon Allah, so I have committed "my affair to Allah".
"And whoever places his trust in Allah, then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has set a measure for all things."
And whoever places his trust in Allah, then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has set a measure for all things.
Sufficient for me is "Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs".
Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs
O Allah, whoever whose need becomes to a created being, then indeed my need and desire is to You.
Praise is to the Lord of the morning, Praise is to the Splitter of the dawn, three times.
And it is permissible as a substitute for lying down, prostration, walking, and speaking, except that lying down is superior.

key_terms.اِضْطَجَعْتُ عَلَى يَمِينِي: Lying down on the right side
key_terms.تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اَللّهِ: I placed my trust in Allah

ai.seo_question: What supplication and Quranic verses should be recited after the two rak'ahs of Fajr according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes reciting the final five verses of Surah Al-Imran (3:178-182) alongside a specific dhikr affirming reliance on Allah, emphasizing the transition from worldly dependence to divine trust after the Fajr sunnah prayers. This practice highlights the Shia emphasis on integrating Quranic recitation with supplication during the quiet moments of the morning, with lying on the right side being the optimal posture for this devotion.
